upgrade_bypass.description: HTTP/2 cleartext (h2c) upgrade smuggling — send Upgrade: h2c to bypass reverse proxy ACLs. The proxy does not understand h2c and forwards the request to the backend, which upgrades and processes requests outside the proxy's access control.

probes.description: h2c upgrade request — if backend returns 101 Switching Protocols, the connection bypasses the reverse proxy's path-based ACL

variables.header:
Upgrade: h2c
HTTP2-Settings: AAMAAABkAAQCAAAAAAIAAAAA
Connection: Upgrade, HTTP2-Settings

probes.description: h2c upgrade with lowercase headers — some proxies only filter capitalized Upgrade

variables.header:
upgrade: h2c
http2-settings: AAMAAABkAAQCAAAAAAIAAAAA
connection: upgrade, http2-settings

connection_header_injection.description: Test if the reverse proxy strips or passes the Connection hop-by-hop header. If it passes Connection: Upgrade, h2c, the backend may upgrade the connection out from under the proxy.

probes.description: Connection: keep-alive, Upgrade — test if the proxy passes hop-by-hop headers to backend
Websocket upgrade to h2c variant — some proxies allow websocket upgrades but not h2c; test if the mechanism works for h2c too

variables.header:
Connection: Upgrade
Upgrade: h2c
Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13
Sec-WebSocket-Key: dGhlIHNhbXBsZSBub25jZQ==

hpack_bomb_dos.description: HTTP/2 HPACK Bomb + Slowloris DoS (Calif Jun 2026). HPACK-compressed headers decompress to huge sizes (5700:1 amplification). Combined with connection hold, causes OOM on default configs of nginx, Apache, IIS, Envoy, Pingora. Detection only — not a finding class, but reveals HTTP/2 is enabled and server memory behavior.

probes.description: Detect HTTP/2 support via upgrade or ALPN — prerequisite for HPACK attacks
